meaning: to personally realise / to deeply appreciate (through experience)
usage: Used to describe understanding or realising something through personal experience
Often expresses deeper, reflective understanding rather than surface knowledge
Commonly paired with 親身 / 慢慢 / 真正 to emphasise lived experience

examples.sentence: 親身經歷之後，我先真正體會到呢份工作嘅壓力。
examples.jyutping: can1 san1 ging1 lik6 zi1 hau6, ngo5 sin1 zan1 zing3 tai2 wui6 dou3 ni1 fan6 gung1 zok3 ge3 aat3 lik6
examples.meaning: Only after experiencing it firsthand did I truly realise the pressure of this job.

examples.sentence: 慢慢做落去，你會體會到點解佢會咁講。
examples.jyutping: maan6 maan6 zou6 lok6 heoi3, nei5 wui5 tai2 wui6 dou3 dim2 gaai2 keoi5 wui5 gam3 gong2
examples.meaning: As you go along, you’ll come to realise why they said that.
